This course introduces students to the performance techniques, pedagogical approaches, and content knowledge essential for teaching brass instruments. Through hands-on laboratory experiences and peer teaching, students will develop foundational performance skills on multiple brass instruments and explore effective strategies for teaching beginners. By the end of the course, students will be able to model and teach basic brass techniques, apply pedagogical principles in classroom and individual settings, and critically reflect on performances and teaching to support continued growth.
course_details.Registration Requirements: There are no registration requirements for this course.
course_details.Learning Objectives:
Course Goal 1 - Performance Skills: Demonstrate foundational performance skills on multiple brass instruments.
• CG1.LO1 Tone Production: Demonstrate characteristic tone production at the beginner level on multiple brass instruments.
• CG1.LO2 Basic Articulation: Demonstrate basic articulation technique on multiple brass instruments.
• CG1.LO3 Aural Skills: Perform on multiple brass instruments without the aid of Western standard music notation (e.g., improvised patterns, repertoire learned by ear, or call and response activities).
• CG1.LO4 Etudes and Exercises: Perform introductory exercises and etudes with beginner-level accuracy on multiple brass instruments using Western standard music notation.
Course Goal 2 - Content Knowledge: Develop a foundational knowledge of brass instrument mechanics and performance practices.
• CG2.LO1 Instrument Mechanics: Explain the basic acoustics and fundamentals of tone production for brass instruments.
• CG2.LO2 Instrument Fingerings: Identify fingerings and concert pitch for the beginner range of each brass instrument.
• CG2.LO3 Equipment: Identify recommended equipment for beginning brass musicians.
• CG2.LO4 Maintenance: Describe basic maintenance for brass instruments.
• CG2.LO5 Brass Traditions: Compare a variety of brass performance traditions.
Course Goal 3 - Pedagogical Skills: Develop foundational skills and strategies for teaching beginner brass musicians.
• CG3.LO1 Learning Sequence: Implement skill-building exercises and learning sequences appropriate for beginning brass musicians.
• CG3.LO2 Diagnostic Skills: Identify common beginning brass performance issues.
• CG3.LO3 Remediation Strategies: Select practice strategies that support the remediation of common beginner brass performance issues.
• CG3.LO4 Feedback: Provide constructive feedback, including suggestions for improvement, to beginning brass musicians.
• CG3.LO5 Instructional Materials: Evaluate how selected repertoire or instructional materials supports the developmental needs of beginning brass musicians.
Course Goal 4 - Reflective Practice: Examine performances and teaching episodes to determine successes and areas for improvement.
• CG4.LO1 Performance Reflection: Reflect critically on one's own and peers' musical performances to support continued artistic growth.
• CG4.LO2 Teaching Reflection: Reflect critically on one's own and peers' teaching episodes to support continued pedagogical growth.
course_details.Teaching Method: This course will include direct instruction, instructor modeling, and lab-based student practice. This course uses a flipped classroom approach so that class meetings can focus on applying technical and pedagogical skills. Students will be expected to transport the university-provided instruments to and from each class, play with classmates during each class, lead selected exercises, and provide constructive feedback to peers.
course_details.Evaluation Method: Students will be evaluated through video-recorded performance assessments on multiple brass instruments, self-reflections, teaching episodes, in-class quizzes, professionalism, and an oral exam.

course_details.Overview of class: The purpose of this course is to stimulate your thinking about your role as a music educator, as well as the role of music in the broader educative experience. In this course you will explore some of the philosophical principles, concepts, and ideas that provide music education with purpose and direction. Grappling with these ideas will improve your knowledge and understanding about music teaching and the actions of music educators. This class will help you articulate a vision for music in schools and a philosophical orientation toward music teaching and learning.

course_details.Overview of class: This course provides perspectives on a variety of contemporary music education practices, including relevant technologies, popular music pedagogy, and critical educational issues. This course focuses on sociocultural and constructivist practices that emphasize student success through student centered, culturally relevant approaches to music.
course_details.Learning Objectives: Students will demonstrate the ability to teach music to students, K-12 settings and community ensembles, using relevant technologies. Students will demonstrate the ability to teach popular music to students in K-12 settings and community ensembles. Classroom writing assignments are based on music teaching pedagogies and approaches, planning, curriculum, assessment, and the sequencing of skills in teaching music across various populations.

course_details.Overview of class: Teaching and administrative principles for elementary and middle school instrumental music programs. Rehearsal dynamics, conducting, rehearsal room management, and pedagogy for school ensembles.
course_details.Registration Requirements: Prerequisite: Must be 3rd year and above and have completed MUSIC_ED 230, 231, 232, 233, 234, 235, or 236. Co-registration requirement in MUSIC ED 314-0.
course_details.Learning Objectives:
1. Develop a philosophy of instrumental music education that could serve as a program mission statement
2. Critically consider the role of the teacher and student in a large ensemble setting
3. Be able to apply elements of direct instruction and constructivist pedagogical approaches
4. Be able to design a teaching plan that emphasizes comprehensive musicianship as a complement to performance skill
5. Observe and develop pedagogical skills for school settings
6. Be able to teach rhythmic and tonal concepts using a sound-to-symbol approach
7. Be able to analyze repertoire for pedagogical purposes
8. Be able to apply cooperative learning approaches through peer teaching and chamber music
9. Be able to apply effective rehearsal strategies in large ensembles
10. Consider approaches for effective classroom management and motivation in instrumental music education
11. Add to their developing professional portfolio

course_details.Overview of class: This course provides an overview of the multifaceted nature of choral teaching and learning in elementary and middle school, setting a foundation for students' construction of their philosophy and practices as a choral music educator. Topics covered include but are not limited to rehearsal techniques, vocal technique, repertoire, curriculum design, classroom management, and the adolescent changing voice. Students will apply the acquired knowledge and skills through assigned projects and practicum placements, which shall be determined at the beginning of the class term. Readings, assignments, and classwork will provide practical tools to ensure that what you do on and off the podium reflects best practices to develop an outstanding, thriving choral program applicable in any teaching format and at any educational level.
course_details.Registration Requirements: Prerequisite: Must be 3rd year or above. Co-registration requirement in MUSIC ED 314.
course_details.Learning Objectives:
After completing this course, students should be able to:
1. Identify and describe essential components of middle school choral pedagogy, including vocal technique principles, sight-singing methodologies, warm-up exercises, rehearsal strategies, and characteristics of the adolescent socioemotional development and changing voice.
2. Explain how culturally responsive repertoire selection, student-centered teaching practices, and developmentally appropriate vocal pedagogy align with their developing philosophy of choral music education.
3. Demonstrate effective, evidence-based rehearsal techniques, classroom management strategies, sight-singing instruction, and warm-up sequences.
4. Evaluate choral repertoire using pre-established criteria to assess appropriateness for middle school voices, difficulty level, musical content, curricular objectives, and pedagogical opportunities.
5. Design comprehensive rehearsal plans and concert programs that demonstrate balanced repertoire choices across diverse styles, languages, and difficulty levels while addressing the needs of changing voices and incorporating effective pedagogical sequences.
6. Develop an original philosophy of choral teaching articulating their core beliefs and pedagogical priorities concerning choral music education.
7. Build a choral program website (ePortfolio) that showcases their philosophy of choral teaching, choral pedagogy, and sample materials.
